submitted.body:
The paper exhibits a nine-vertex, twenty-edge graph, obtained from K_(3,3,3) by deleting seven edges. Its upper irredundance number is three, and its nine maximum irredundant sets form P_9 under the required vertex-exchange adjacency. Two small tables provide a hand-checkable proof, accompanied by the Lean certificate. This refutes the path part of the conjecture. The cycle part and the case P_6 remain open in this work; the bounded exhaustive-search claims are distinct from the formalized counterexample.

**Result and scope:** part (i) of the conjecture (paths) is false: P_9 is an IR-graph; computationally 9 is the minimum order of a graph whose IR-graph is a path of order >= 3 and P_7, P_8, P_9 occur at order 9; part (ii) (cycles) and P_6 remain open

**Complete proof and verification sources:** [The path P_9 is an IR-graph: a nine-vertex counterexample to the Mynhardt-Roux non-IR conjecture for paths](https://mathdb.com/abs/2611.00056) · [PDF](https://mathdb.com/pdf/2611.00056v1).

The paper page includes the supplementary proof-source JSON attachment and `extract_sources.py`, which reconstruct the archived proof and verification sources. The linked paper gives the complete rigorous argument and specifies exactly which statements are formalized.
